# Agent tools reference

The 16 `finance_*` tools. One definition each, in `src/hermes_finance/tooldefs.py`, shared by the Hermes plugin (`hermes_plugin/`) and the MCP server (`finance mcp`, and `/mcp` on `finance serve`). A read tool answers exactly what its `finance <command> --json` prints.

- **read**: opens the database read-only and never calls Plaid. Listed everywhere.
- **action** (`finance_sync`): syncs with Plaid now. It changes nothing you entered, so it runs without an approval, except `refresh=true` on a paid Plaid plan (Plaid bills each refresh), which needs one.
- **write**: in the Hermes plugin, Hermes asks for your approval first (and blocks it where nobody can answer). Over MCP these are listed only after `finance mcp allow-writes on`, and a call is only saved as a pending action you approve in Settings.

The MCP server's instructions to every client:

> hermes-finance: the owner's own money data from a local database, read-only. Amounts use the app's sign: spend and money out are positive, refunds and income negative. Use a category's exact name (finance_spend with by=category lists them); never guess one. Dates are local. In human-facing text, use $ and thousands separators. Round to cents, omit cents for whole dollars, and keep two decimals otherwise. Put an ASCII minus before $ for negatives and suppress it for rounded zero. Keep numeric tool arguments and JSON fields numeric.

| Tool | Kind | Same as |
|---|---|---|
| [`finance_spend`](#finance-spend) | read | `finance spend --json` |
| [`finance_budget_status`](#finance-budget-status) | read | `finance budget-status --json` |
| [`finance_transactions`](#finance-transactions) | read | `finance txns --json` |
| [`finance_networth`](#finance-networth) | read | `finance networth --json` |

## `finance_spend` {#finance-spend}

Spending total (income and transfers excluded, refunds netted) for a period, with the previous equal period; optionally grouped. Default: this month. Spend is positive, refunds negative.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance spend --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `month` | string | no |  | one month, YYYY-MM (not with since/until) |
| `since` | string | no |  | from: Nd (the last N days, today included) or YYYY-MM-DD |
| `until` | string | no |  | through YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (default today) |
| `category` | string | no |  | category name, case-insensitive; must exist |
| `merchant` | string | no |  | part of the merchant or transaction name |
| `account` | string | no |  | account: last digits, name, or part of the name |
| `limit` | integer | no | min 1; max 500 | most rows/groups returned (default 50) |
| `by` | string | no | one of `category`, `merchant`, `month`, `account` | group the total |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "month": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "one month, YYYY-MM (not with since/until)"
    },
    "since": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "from: Nd (the last N days, today included) or YYYY-MM-DD"
    },
    "until": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "through YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive (default today)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "category name, case-insensitive; must exist"
    },
    "merchant": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "part of the merchant or transaction name"
    },
    "account": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "account: last digits, name, or part of the name"
    },
    "limit": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 500,
      "description": "most rows/groups returned (default 50)"
    },
    "by": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "group the total",
      "enum": [
        "category",
        "merchant",
        "month",
        "account"
      ]
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_budget_status` {#finance-budget-status}

Each monthly budget cap and group budget: spent, bills still due, left, % used, status (ok/warn/over), pace projection; uncapped spend and totals. A cap in a group budget is counted: false; group_rest: a capped group's uncapped spend. Default: this month.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance budget-status --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `month` | string | no |  | YYYY-MM (default this month) |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "month": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "YYYY-MM (default this month)"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_transactions` {#finance-transactions}

Transactions, newest first, with category and who set it (user/rule/ai/plaid/default). Filters narrow. Default: all history, 50 rows. Money out is positive, money in negative.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance txns --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `month` | string | no |  | one month, YYYY-MM (not with since/until) |
| `since` | string | no |  | from: Nd (the last N days, today included) or YYYY-MM-DD |

| `category` | string | no |  | category name, case-insensitive; must exist |
| `merchant` | string | no |  | part of the merchant or transaction name |
| `account` | string | no |  | account: last digits, name, or part of the name |
| `limit` | integer | no | min 1; max 500 | most rows/groups returned (default 50) |
| `search` | string | no |  | text in the name, merchant, category, account, bank, AI note, the user's note or a tag, or the amount (465.10) |
| `flagged` | boolean | no |  | only rows the AI flagged and the user hasn't decided |

## `finance_networth` {#finance-networth}

    }

## `finance_bills` {#finance-bills}

Recurring bills and subscriptions expected in the next N days (overdue ones included): amount (an estimate and usual range when it changes), cadence, status, detected or tracked, last paid from, outlier; plus monthly totals.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance bills --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `next` | string | no |  | how far ahead: Nd, 0d-730d (default 14d) |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "next": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "how far ahead: Nd, 0d-730d (default 14d)"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_loans` {#finance-loans}

Loans: remaining balance, APR, monthly payment, payoff estimate, last matched payment.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance loans --json`.

No arguments.

## `finance_holdings` {#finance-holdings}

Investment accounts and holdings: value, quantity, price, % of the portfolio; portfolio changes.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance holdings --json`.

No arguments.

## `finance_cashflow` {#finance-cashflow}

Income vs spending per month, oldest first, ending with this month (income positive).

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance cashflow --json`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |

| `months` | integer | no | min 1; max 120 | how many months (default 6) |

  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "months": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 120,
      "description": "how many months (default 6)"
    }

## `finance_status` {#finance-status}

Connected banks: status, errors, last sync, accounts with balances, bank connection slots used.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance status --json`.

No arguments.

## `finance_goals` {#finance-goals}

The user's goals: Save up (an account, part of one, or logged entries), Pay off (a loan or card) and Monthly savings (income minus spending vs a target): progress, % and what's left, pace. Goals never change any total.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance goals --json`.

No arguments.

## `finance_rules` {#finance-rules}

Categorization rules, newest first: what each matches (label), its category, who made it (user/ai), how many transactions it matches now; counts; and suggested rules (merchants the user filed by hand 2+ times). Read-only.

Kind: read. Same answer as `finance rules --json`.

No arguments.

## `finance_sync` {#finance-sync}

Sync now: pull what the banks already sent Plaid (new transactions, balances) and say what changed, with data_age. refresh=true first asks the banks for fresh data, if Settings allows it; on a paid Plaid plan that needs the user's approval.

Kind: action.

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `refresh` | boolean | no |  | first ask the banks for fresh data (Plaid's refresh; default false). New items land a few minutes later: sync again then |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "refresh": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "first ask the banks for fresh data (Plaid's refresh; default false). New items land a few minutes later: sync again then"
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_set_category` {#finance-set-category}

File one transaction under a category, as the user's decision (rules and the AI never change it). Needs the user's approval.

Kind: write (needs approval).

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `transaction_id` | string | yes |  | the transaction_id from finance_transactions |
| `category` | string | yes |  | category name, case-insensitive; must exist |
| `note` | string | no |  | optional note kept with the decision |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "transaction_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "the transaction_id from finance_transactions"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "category name, case-insensitive; must exist"
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "optional note kept with the decision"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "transaction_id",
    "category"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_add_rule` {#finance-add-rule}

Always file transactions whose merchant name (or name) matches a pattern under a category; re-files the matching ones now. Regex (case-insensitive search) by default; a pattern matching no transaction is refused. Needs the user's approval.

Kind: write (needs approval).

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | string | yes |  | regex searched in the name (or the whole name, with match=exact) |
| `category` | string | yes |  | category name, case-insensitive; must exist |
| `field` | string | no | one of `merchant_name`, `name` | what to match (default merchant_name) |
| `match` | string | no | one of `regex`, `exact` | regex (default) or exact (the whole name, case-insensitive) |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "pattern": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "regex searched in the name (or the whole name, with match=exact)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "category name, case-insensitive; must exist"
    },
    "field": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "what to match (default merchant_name)",
      "enum": [
        "merchant_name",
        "name"
      ]
    },
    "match": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "regex (default) or exact (the whole name, case-insensitive)",
      "enum": [
        "regex",
        "exact"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "pattern",
    "category"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_set_cap` {#finance-set-cap}

Set a spending category's monthly budget cap, or clear it with null. Needs the user's approval.

Kind: write (needs approval).

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | string | yes |  | spending category name, case-insensitive |
| `monthly_cap` | number or null | yes | min 0; max 100000 | the cap in dollars, or null to clear it |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "spending category name, case-insensitive"
    },
    "monthly_cap": {
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ],
      "minimum": 0,
      "maximum": 100000,
      "description": "the cap in dollars, or null to clear it"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "category",
    "monthly_cap"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>

## `finance_track_bill` {#finance-track-bill}

Track a merchant as a bill by hand (track), change a bill's schedule or amount (update), or stop tracking one (stop: a detected one is no longer listed). A bill is the merchant: its charges on any account count. Needs the user's approval.

Kind: write (needs approval).

| Argument | Type | Required | Limits | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes | one of `track`, `update`, `stop` | track, update or stop |
| `merchant` | string | yes |  | the merchant's name as finance_transactions shows it (exact, or a unique case-insensitive match) |
| `every` | string | no | one of `1w`, `2w`, `1m`, `2m`, `3m`, `6m`, `1y` | the schedule: 2w, 1m, 2m, 3m, 6m or 1y (also 1w); default: the detected one, else 1m |
| `varies` | boolean | no |  | true: the amount changes each time (a utility); default: from the category |
| `usually` | number or array or null (items: number) | no | min items 1; max items 2 | what a bill that changes usually is: an amount, or [low, high] (null clears it) |

<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "track, update or stop",
      "enum": [
        "track",
        "update",
        "stop"
      ]
    },
    "merchant": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "the merchant's name as finance_transactions shows it (exact, or a unique case-insensitive match)"
    },
    "every": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "the schedule: 2w, 1m, 2m, 3m, 6m or 1y (also 1w); default: the detected one, else 1m",
      "enum": [
        "1w",
        "2w",
        "1m",
        "2m",
        "3m",
        "6m",
        "1y"
      ]
    },
    "varies": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "true: the amount changes each time (a utility); default: from the category"
    },
    "usually": {
      "type": [
        "number",
        "array",
        "null"
      ],
      "items": {
        "type": "number"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "maxItems": 2,
      "description": "what a bill that changes usually is: an amount, or [low, high] (null clears it)"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action",
    "merchant"
  ],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```

</details>
